transcript: If today was your last day on Earth, what would you do? Would you wake up earlier, just to watch the sunrise one last time? Would you call the person you haven't spoken to in years, just to hear their voice again? Would you step outside barefoot, feel the grass under your feet, and realize you spent most of your life rushing past the little things that made it beautiful? Would you sit with your family, no phones, no distractions, just the sound of their laughter filling the air? Would you hold someone a little longer, knowing this is the last time your arms will ever feel their warmth? Or would you regret how much time you spent worried about things that never really mattered? The opinions of people who won't even remember your name, the stress over money that won't follow you past today, the moments you traded for a future you never got to see. The truth is, one day, this won't be a question, it will be real. And when that day comes, you won't be thinking about success, about status, about the things you owned. You'll be thinking about love, about the time you had, about whether you truly lived. So why wait until the last day to start appreciating it?
